task.title: Stop shipping the full commentaries index on first paint
task.description: Lazy-load the four collapsible book sections in /api/index instead of pre-rendering all four, and replace repeated inline style attributes with CSS classes plus onclick handlers with event delegation. Must preserve verse-range rendering and the no-code-to-add-a-commentary property.
deliverables: New or modified handler serving per-section fragments
acceptance: Index still reaches every author, book and homily
task.scale: 1 Go handler, 1 template, 1 stylesheet, ~7400 handlers and ~10700 style attrs to remove, 4 section fragments

agent_sessions.what: Restructure the index handler to serve per-book-section fragments with htmx lazy triggers
agent_sessions.shape: Feature — new endpoint shape, new fragments, behavioural change

agent_sessions.what: Replace 10,698 inline style attrs with CSS classes and 7,439 onclick handlers with delegation
agent_sessions.shape: Multi-file change — template plus stylesheet, mechanical but wide

agent_sessions.what: Verify verse ranges still render across reader, /api/index, /api/scripture-references, /api/homilies
agent_sessions.shape: Exploration / audit — curl and inspect four link sites
Multi-file change — one to three rework rounds

drivers: Event delegation must reconstruct handler arguments now encoded per-element in onclick
formatCoverageRange() fallback-book gotcha spans four call sites; a miss renders ranges empty and is silent
Adding a commentary must still require no code, so no hardcoded author or book list
risks: Delegation rewrite touches loadTheophylactCommentary and showCanonModal, ~7000 call sites between them — a wrong argument shape breaks commentary loading everywhere at once
Lazy sections may change CLS rather than improve it if fragment height is unreserved
Verse ranges failing silently is the highest-risk regression and is not caught by a green page load
notes: Largest ticket in the epic and the one with real regression risk. S2 is mechanical and could ship independently of S1 if the maintainer wants the win split into two commits.
